title: Names in pairs
hookLine: the First and Last, the Manifest and Hidden, the Withholder and Expander
tomorrow: an old man with no children asks for an heir. which Name?

cards: At noon the stars are all still up there. Daylight doesn't erase them; it hides them. Something can be completely present and completely out of sight at once.
Dadi's first night in the new room, Amira finds her by the window, eyes wet, smiling. "Sad or happy?" Amira asks.
Dadi says: "Both, beta. Why does it have to be one?" The Qur'an has been saying that about Allah all along.

teach.h: THE FIRST AND THE LAST, AT ONCE.
teach.b: Surah al-Hadid, in Pickthall's words: "He is the First and the Last, and the Outward and the Inward; and He is Knower of all things." Not first and then later last. Both, at once.

In a du'a from Sahih Muslim, the Prophet, peace be upon him, unfolds it: You are the First, nothing before You; the Last, nothing after You; the Outward, nothing above You; the Inward, nothing beneath You.
Other Names travel in pairs too.
Surah al-Baqarah: "Allah straiteneth and enlargeth." The Withholder and the Expander, Al-Qabid and Al-Basit.

teach.h: SAY THE PAIR, NOT THE HALF.
teach.b: Scholars of the Names advise saying such pairs together, so that neither half becomes the whole picture. A lean month isn't a verdict; a good month isn't a prize.
The same hand holds both. And this week's Names were already doing it. The Originator who begins, the Inheritor to whom it all returns.
The Everlasting who stays, the Patient who waits. Here's the thing to tell a friend: in Islam some Names are meant to be said as a pair, the way Dadi answered.

how: Muslims often say paired Names together in remembrance, al-Qabid with al-Basit, ad-Darr with an-Nafi', and recite 57:3 among the Names of the First and the Last.

o: a Name repeated twice to make it stronger
Names said together so neither half stands alone
two Names that cancel each other out in a du'a

games.q: the week's Names — tap the pairs.

s: the Inward means Allah is absent or far away
He is the Outward and the Inward at once: present and unseen, like stars at noon.
Surah al-Hadid calls Him the First and the Last
"He is the First and the Last, and the Outward and the Inward."

games.q: your uncle's shop had a great month, then a dead one. he asks you, half joking, if God is mad at him now. what do the paired Names say?
o: the same hand withholds and expands; a lean month isn't a verdict.
a good month means He's pleased, and a dead month means He's angry.
money isn't in Allah's hands at all; it's just how the market goes.
games.why: "Allah straiteneth and enlargeth." the pair is said together so neither half, the lean or the full, gets read as the whole picture.

practice: Close your eyes and hold one pair for the whole sit. On the in-breath, the First; on the out-breath, the Last. When the mind tries to pick one, let both be true at once, without choosing between them.

wordCard.voice: Names in pairs: the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward, said together so neither half stands alone.

orig.note: Arabic: the First and the Last, the opening pair of 57:3.

carryVoice: For the week's end: he holds both, the lean month and the full one, the sad and the glad. A week of names, gathered.

sources.q: He is the First and the Last, and the Outward and the Inward; and He is Knower of all things.
